title: Aarlaghey bee
description: Ten short stories about cooking and food on the Isle of Man: a cooking contest, blackberries, goats' cheese, spices, a Manx recipe class, kitchen science, a harvest supper, school dinners, wild mushrooms and a winter picnic.

lessons.title: Y roortys coagyrey
lessons.summary: Imelda Fairweather, a cook in Ramsey, takes part in a competitive TV cooking contest; she is emotional and her voice shakes, she burns a sauce by not watching the heating and a judge finds it unpalatable, but her coach Cosmo Hartigan helps her, and she is successful in the last week.
lessons.text:
Ta Imelda Fairweather ny coagyrey ayns thie-bee beg ec y phurt ayns Rhumsaa. Rish feed blein, t'ee er ve coagyrey son sleih elley, agh cha row ee rieau ayns roortys. 'Sy tourey shoh chaie, hug ee lettyr gys roortys coagyrey er y çhellveeish, as hooar ee lettyr erash: v'ee goaill ayrn ayn.

Ta'n roortys shoh feer cohirreydagh. Ta queig persoonyn jeig ayn ec y toshiaght, as dagh shiaghtin ta fer jeu goll magh. Ta greinneyder ec dagh persoon. She Cosmo Hartigan greinneyder Imelda. Va Cosmo hene ladoosagh ayns roortys cohirreydagh elley roish jeih bleeaney, as nish t'eh ny ghreinneyder.

“Ta schlei vooar ayd,” dooyrt Cosmo rish Imelda 'sy chied shiaghtin. “Agh cha nel schlei dy liooar ayns roortys. Ta ram sleih ayn, as ta ram schlei oc. Lhisagh oo ve lajer myrgeddin.”

Va Imelda feer ennaghtagh. Tra va sleih jeeaghyn urree, va'n coraa eck craa, as cha dod ee loayrt dy mie. “Va mee ennaghtagh rieau,” dooyrt ee rish Cosmo. “Tra ta aggle orrym, ta my choraa goll beg.”

'Sy nah hiaghtin, va'n obbyr doillee. Va er dagh persoon eeast y aarlaghey ayns three feed minnid. Ren Imelda toshiaght mie. Agh cha row ee jeeaghyn er y çhiassaghey, as va'n aile ro lajer. Losht y soo eck. Va'n soo doo, as va blass loshtit er.

Ghow fer jeh ny briwnyn blass jeh'n soo. “T'eh meevlasstal,” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n eeast mie, agh ta'n soo meevlasstal.” Va Imelda er-gerrey da keayney.

'Sy fastyr, loayr Cosmo rish Imelda. “Losht dagh coagyrey red ennagh keayrt ennagh,” dooyrt eh. “Agh lhisagh oo jeeaghyn er y çhiassaghey dagh traa. As lhisagh oo geddyn y choraa ayd reesht. Loayr nish, dy feer ard.” Loayr Imelda dy ard, as va'n coraa eck lajer.

'Sy shiaghtin s'jerree, cha row agh three persoonyn faagit. Ren Imelda eeast as praaseyn, as soo noa. Va'n çhiassaghey kiart, as cha losht red erbee. Loayr ee rish ny briwnyn ayns coraa lajer. Hug ny briwnyn y chied ynnyd jee. V'ee ladoosagh! Va Imelda ennaghtagh reesht, agh nish v'ee ennaghtagh er-y-fa dy row ee booiagh.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi greinneyder Imelda?
She Cosmo Hartigan greinneyder Imelda.
Cre haghyr da'n choraa eck tra va sleih jeeaghyn urree?
Va'n coraa eck craa.
Cre'n fa losht y soo eck?
Losht y soo er-y-fa nagh row ee jeeaghyn er y çhiassaghey.
Cre dooyrt y briw mychione y soo?
Dooyrt eh dy row y soo meevlasstal.
Row Imelda ladoosagh 'sy jerrey?
Va. Hooar ee y chied ynnyd.

lessons.title: Smeir er y chrongan
lessons.summary: Prudence Ashcroft takes her daughter's son Jethro to pick blackberries on a hillock above Laxey: they walk a leafy lane, a spike of the bramble gives him a small wound, he finds a worm in a berry and insects on the leaves, climbs a big rock for the views, and at home they eat the blackberries with sugar and milk.
lessons.text:
Ec jerrey dagh tourey, ta Prudence Ashcroft goll magh dy hroggal smeir. Ta Prudence cummal ayns Laksaa. Jiu, ta Jethro marish. She mac e inneen eh, as t'eh jeih bleeaney d'eash.

Hie ad magh ass y valley er raad beg duillagagh. Va biljyn ard as duillagagh er dagh çheu jeh'n raad, as va'n raad doo as feayr fo ny duillagyn. Ec jerrey y raad duillagagh, va crongan glass, as er y chrongan va ram lossreeyn smeyr.

“Jeeagh er ny smeir!” dooyrt Jethro. Va ny smeir mooar as doo. Ghow eh smeyr, as hug eh ayns e veeal eh. “T'eh millish!” dooyrt eh.

“Kiarail,” dooyrt Prudence. “Ta birryn er ny lossreeyn smeyr. Ta birr geyre er dagh banglane.”

Ec y traa cheddin, hie birr stiagh ayns laue Jethro. Va lhott beg jiarg er e laue, as va fuill ayn. Ren Jethro keayney son tammylt. “Cha nel eh agh lhott beg,” dooyrt Prudence, as hug ee ushtey glen er y lhott. Lurg minnid ny ghaa, cha row Jethro keayney ny smoo.

V'ad troggal smeir son oor. Eisht, dooyrt Jethro: “Ta peisht 'sy smeyr shoh!” Va peisht veg vane çheet magh ass y smeyr. Va beisteigyn er ny duillagyn myrgeddin. “Ta ny peishtyn as ny beisteigyn gee ny smeir, myr ta shin hene,” dooyrt Prudence. “Ny gow agh ny smeir glen. Faag ny smeir elley da ny beisteigyn.”

Er mullagh y chrongan va carrick vooar. “Vod mee drappal er y charrick?” dooyrt Jethro. “Foddee oo,” dooyrt Prudence, “agh kiarail. Cha jean mee hene drappal. Ta my chassyn ro henn son drappal.”

Ren Jethro drappal seose er y charrick. Veih mullagh y charrick, va reayrtyssyn aalin ayn: y keayn gorrym, y valley ayns y ghlion, as ny sleityn. “Ta ny reayrtyssyn shoh share na'n çhellveeish!” dooyrt eh.

Ec y thie, ren Prudence ny smeir y ghlenney. Hug ee shugyr as bainney orroo, as v'ad gee ny smeir ry-cheilley. Va laue Jethro foast jiarg, agh cha row eh smooinaghtyn er y lhott ny smoo.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi eh Jethro?
She mac inneen Prudence eh.
Cre'n raad hie ad gys y chrongan?
Hie ad er raad beg duillagagh.
Cre ren birr da laue Jethro?
Hie birr stiagh ayns e laue, as va lhott beg er.
Cre va 'sy smeyr?
Va peisht veg vane 'sy smeyr.
Cre va Jethro fakin veih mullagh y charrick?
Va reayrtyssyn aalin ayn: y keayn, y valley as ny sleityn.

lessons.title: Caashey goayr ayns Nalbin
lessons.summary: Petra Lindqvist bought a glen farm in Scotland abandoned forty years before; the builder Ruben Okafor rebuilds the ruined house, a storm destroys the goats' shed, mice get at the cheese, the goat droppings feed the garden, and an eagle over the mountain makes her keep the young goats in at night.
lessons.text:
Roish queig bleeaney, chionnee Petra Lindqvist thalloo ayns glion eddyr ny sleityn ayns Nalbin. Va shenn thie er y thalloo, agh va'n thie ny tholtan. Va'n lught-thie va cummal ayn er hreigeil y thalloo roish daeed blein, as cha row peiagh erbee er ve cummal 'sy thie rish daeed blein. Va'n thalloo treigit, as va lughee ayns dagh shamyr jeh'n tholtan.

Cha row Petra goll dy hreigeil y thalloo reesht. Hooar ee troggeyder, Ruben Okafor, as ren Ruben y thie y hroggal reesht. Va'n troggeyder gobbraghey er y thie son blein slane. Ren eh ny boallaghyn as y mullagh noa. Nish, cha nel y thie ny tholtan ny smoo.

Ta goair ec Petra. Ta feed goayr eck, as ta ee jannoo caashey veih bainney ny goair. Ta'n caashey eck feer vie. Dagh shiaghtin, t'ee goaill block mooar caashey gys y margey ayns y valley mooar, as ta sleih kionnaghey eh.

'Sy nah gheurey, haink sterrym mooar. Va'n thie beg va ny goair cummal ayn scrysst. Va'n mullagh echey er y thalloo, as va ny boallaghyn brisht. Haink Ruben y troggeyder reesht, as ren eh thie noa son ny goair 'syn ynnyd va scrysst.

Va lughee foast ayns y thie. Ren ny lughee goaill toshiaght gee y caashey. Ren ad towl ayns block mooar caashey! Eisht, chionnee Petra kayt. Nish, cha nel ny lughee çheet stiagh ny smoo.

Ta keck ny goair mie son y thalloo. Dagh arragh, ta Petra goaill y keck veih thie ny goair, as t'ee cur y keck er y gharey. Ta ny lossreeyn gaase dy mie 'sy gharey.

Ta urley cummal er y slieau ard ec kione y ghlion. Ny keayrtyn, ta Petra fakin yn urley ard 'syn aer. Ta'n urley mooar as lajer, as t'eh gee ushagyn as beiyn beggey. Ayns y tourey, ta goair veggey aeg ec Petra. Er-y-fa shen, dagh oie, ta Petra goll lesh ny goair veggey stiagh ayns thie ny goair, son dy vel ad sauçhey veih'n urley.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n traa va'n thalloo treigit?
Va'n thalloo treigit roish daeed blein.
Quoi ren y tholtan y hroggal reesht?
Ren y troggeyder, Ruben Okafor, eh y hroggal reesht.
Cre ren y sterrym?
Va thie ny goair scrysst ec y sterrym.
Cre ren ny lughee?
Ren ny lughee gee y caashey, as ren ad towl ayns block caashey.
Cre'n fa ta Petra cur keck ny goair er y gharey?
Er-y-fa dy vel y keck mie son y thalloo.

lessons.title: Raad ny spiosyn
lessons.summary: At the museum in Douglas, Linus Carver gives a talk on the history of spices: riders carried spices and silk on horses to the Mediterranean countries and exchanged them for gold, discoverers with a compass and the king's permission made long voyages to find a sea road, and a girl in the audience asks what they expected to find.
lessons.text:
Ta Linus Carver gobbraghey ayns y taishbynys ayns Doolish. Jiu, t'eh loayrt rish possan dy leih mychione shennaghys ny spiosyn. Ta spiosyn ayns dagh shapp nish, as cha nel ad deyr. Agh roish ymmodee keeadyn, va spiosyn feer deyr ayns yn Oarpey, ny smoo deyr na airh.

“Va ny spiosyn gaase foddey ersooyl, 'sy niar,” dooyrt Linus. “Va dellalyn goll lesh spiosyn as sheeidey veih'n Injey as veih çheeraghyn elley 'sy niar. Va'n sheeidey aalin as bog, as va sleih berçhagh laccal sheeidey son nyn eaddagh.”

Ren Linus soilshaghey kaart er y voalley. “Va markee goll er cabbil harrish ny thallooyn mooarey,” dooyrt eh. “She obbyr doillee v'ayn. Va'n markiagh goll rish mee er mee, as ny keayrtyn cha row eh çheet erash. 'Sy jerrey, haink ny markee gys ny çheeraghyn meanvooiragh. Ayns ny buill vooarey meanvooiragh, ren ad coonrey ny spiosyn as y sheeidey son airh as argid. Va coonrey er ve ny obbyr vie, son va'n coonrey cur ram argid da ny dellalyn.”

“Agh va ny çheeraghyn sheear laccal raad elley,” dooyrt Linus. “Cha row ad laccal argid y eeck da dellalyn meanvooiragh. Shen y fa ren ny fowderyn goaill toshiaght. Ren fowder veih Portugal marrinys mygeayrt yn Affrick. Va'n varrinys shen foddey as doillee, as v'eh er y cheayn rish ymmodee meeaghyn.”

Ghow Linus combaase shenn magh ass kishtey. “She combaase eh shoh,” dooyrt eh. “Cha row ny fowderyn abyl goll er marrinys foddey gyn combaase. Lesh y chombaase, v'ad toiggal c'raad va'n twoaie.”

“Cha dod ny fowderyn goll er y varrinys gyn creeaght,” dooyrt eh. “Va creeaght veih'n ree feme orroo. Hug y ree creeaght daue, as hug eh lhongyn daue, son v'eh laccal ny spiosyn as yn airh myrgeddin.”

Va inneen aeg, Saffron, ny soie ayns y chied rane. “Cre va ny fowderyn jerkal dy gheddyn?” dooyrt ee.

“Feysht vie,” dooyrt Linus. “V'ad jerkal dy gheddyn raad noa er y cheayn gys ny spiosyn. Hooar ad y raad shen. Agh hooar ad thallooyn nagh row ad jerkal myrgeddin. Cha row fys oc er ny thallooyn shen roie.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad va ny dellalyn geddyn spiosyn as sheeidey?
V'ad geddyn ad veih'n Injey as veih çheeraghyn elley 'sy niar.
Cre ren ny markee ayns ny buill vooarey meanvooiragh?
Ren ad coonrey ny spiosyn as y sheeidey son airh as argid.
Cre'n fa va combaase feme er ny fowderyn?
Lesh y chombaase, v'ad toiggal c'raad va'n twoaie.
Quoi hug creeaght da ny fowderyn?
Hug y ree creeaght daue.
Cre va ny fowderyn jerkal dy gheddyn?
V'ad jerkal dy gheddyn raad noa er y cheayn gys ny spiosyn.

lessons.title: Arran 'sy vrastyl Ghaelg
lessons.summary: In his diary, Konrad Albrecht, a German learning Manx in Douglas, describes a Friday class where the teacher Orla Penhallow brings an old cookbook published in 1950: the class recites a chapter about bread, he struggles with diphthongs, learns where the subject goes and that Manx has no neuter and no accusative, and the dough sticks to his hands until he stretches it out.
lessons.text:
Jeheiney

She Konrad Albrecht my ennym. Ta mee er ve ynsaghey Gaelg rish blein nish. Ta mee cummal ayns Doolish, agh she Germaanish my hengey hene. Dagh Jeheiney, ta mee goll gys brastyl Ghaelg. She Orla Penhallow yn ynseyder ain.

'Sy fastyr jiu, va'n vrastyl anchasley. Haink Orla lesh shenn lioar mychione coagyrey. Va'n lioar soilshaghit ayns Doolish 'sy vlein 1950. Va jallooyn soilshaghit er ram duillagyn, as va'n Ghaelg aalin. “Cha nel monney lioaryn coagyrey soilshaghit ayns Gaelg,” dooyrt Orla, “as shoh yn lioar share.”

Ren Orla y lioar y osley ec y shiaghtoo cabdil. She cabdil mychione arran v'ayn. “Jiu, ta shin goll dy lhaih y chabdil shoh,” dooyrt ee, “as eisht ta shin goll dy aarlaghey yn arran.”

Hoshiaght, va shin aaloayrt y cabdil, as va dagh persoon aaloayrt ayrn jeh. Tra ren mee aaloayrt my ayrn, va mee loayrt dy moal, son va ny fockleyn doillee dou. Ta daaghooaght ayns ram fockleyn Gaelg, myr “aile” as “oie”. Cha nel ny daaghooaghtyn shoh ayns Germaanish, as cha nel eh aashagh dou y daaghooaght y ghra dy kiart.

Eisht, loayr Orla mychione grammeydys. “Ayns Gaelg, ta'n fockle ‘ren’ ny ‘ta’ çheet hoshiaght, as eisht y commagh,” dooyrt ee. “Ayns ‘Ren y ben yn arran’, she ‘y ben’ y commagh.” Ayns Germaanish, ta'n commagh çheet hoshiaght dy mennick. Er-y-fa shen, ta'n raa Gaelg doillee dou ny keayrtyn.

Ta fockleyn naeear ayns Germaanish: cha nel ad ‘fer’ ny ‘ben’. Agh cha nel fockle naeear erbee ayns Gaelg. As ta cassidagh ayns Germaanish as ayns Ladjyn, agh cha nel cassidagh ayns Gaelg nish. Dooyrt mee rish Orla: “Gyn naeear as gyn cassidagh, ta Gaelg ny s'aashagh na Germaanish!” Ren ee gearey.

'Sy jerrey, ren shin yn arran. Ren mee y meein as yn ushtey y vestey. Va'n arran fliugh, as ren eh lhiann rish my laueyn. “Cur meein er dty laueyn, Konrad, as cha jean eh lhiann rhyt,” dooyrt Orla. “Nish, sheeyn eh magh.” Ren mee yn arran y heeyn magh er y voayrd. Va'n arran sheeynit lhean.

Tra va'n arran jeant, dooyrt mee: “Ta'n arran aym blasstal.” Dooyrt Orla dy row y raa shen grammeydagh kiart. Ta mee booiagh: ta'n arran aym mie, as ta my Ghaelg grammeydagh!

Feyshtyn:
C'raad as cre'n traa va'n lioar soilshaghit?
Va'n lioar soilshaghit ayns Doolish 'sy vlein 1950.
Cre va ayns y shiaghtoo cabdil?
Va'n cabdil mychione arran.
Vel daaghooaghtyn ayns Germaanish myr ta ayns Gaelg?
Cha nel. Cha nel ny daaghooaghtyn shoh ayns Germaanish.
Vel cassidagh ayns Gaelg nish?
Cha nel. Ta cassidagh ayns Germaanish as ayns Ladjyn, agh cha nel ayns Gaelg.
Cre dooyrt Orla tra va'n arran lhiann rish laueyn Konrad?
Dooyrt ee rish Konrad meein y chur er e laueyn.

lessons.title: Oaylleeaght as soo fungys
lessons.summary: Hester Bramwell, who studied engineering, cooks mushroom soup with her son Casimir and answers his questions: the gas is methane, the xenon in the car lamp does not burn, mushrooms are eukaryotes with branching threads under the ground, the iron pot is conductive and its wide base gives it stability, the shiny lid reflects heat, water drips from it, and the heat of the flame is variable.
lessons.text:
Ta Hester Bramwell cummal ayns Purt ny h-Inshey marish e vac, Casimir. Ren Hester jeshaghteyrys y ynsaghey ec y colleish, as nish t'ee gobbraghey myr jeshaghteyr. Ta Casimir daa vlein jeig d'eash, as t'eh laccal jeshaghteyrys y ynsaghey myrgeddin. T'eh cur feyshtyn er e voir dagh traa.

Jesarn shoh chaie, va Hester as Casimir jannoo soo fungys son y shibbyr. Ren Hester y gass y lostey. “Cre ta 'sy gass?” dooyrt Casimir.

“She meetane eh,” dooyrt Hester. “Ta meetane lostey dy mie, as t'eh cur çhiass mooar. Agh cha nel soilshey ec meetane, as cha nel blass echey. Shen y fa ta stoo elley currit 'sy gass, son dy vel fys ain tra ta'n meetane çheet magh.”

“As y soilshey mooar ayns y gleashtan ain?” dooyrt Casimir. “Dooyrt oo dy vel gass ayn.”

“Ta,” dooyrt Hester. “She xenon eh. Agh cha nel xenon myr meetane. Cha nel xenon lostey. Tra ta lectraghys goll trooid y xenon, t'eh cur soilshey bane.”

Eisht, ren Casimir ny fungyssyn y yiarrey. “Vel fungys myr losserey?” dooyrt eh.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Hester. “She eukaryote eh y fungys, as she eukaryote eh y losserey, as she eukaryote oo hene! Ta ny killagyn ec dagh eukaryote anchasley rish killagyn bacteyryn. Agh cha nel y fungys myr losserey ayns aghtyn elley. Fo'n thalloo, ta snaueyn banglaneagh ec y fungys. Ta ny snaueyn banglaneagh shen goll foddey fo'n thalloo.”

Hug Hester ny fungyssyn 'sy saagh yiarn. “Ta yiarn leeideilagh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n çhiass goll trooid dy tappee. Agh cha nel fuygh leeideilagh: er-y-fa shen, ta laue fuygh er y saagh.” Ta bun lhean ec y saagh, as er-y-fa shen ta fondid echey. “Ta fondid scanshoil ayns jeshaghteyrys,” dooyrt Hester. “Gyn fondid, harragh y saagh harrish.”

Va mullagh airhey er y saagh. “Ta'n mullagh shoh aahoilshaghey y çhiass sheese 'sy soo,” dooyrt Hester. “T'eh aahoilshaghey y soilshey myrgeddin: jeeagh, ta dty eddin aynjee!” Lurg tammylt, va ushtey drigey veih'n mullagh. “Ta'n ushtey goll seose myr gaal, as eisht t'eh drigey sheese reesht,” dooyrt Hester.

Va'n aile ceaghlagh: ny keayrtyn mooar, ny keayrtyn beg. “Ta'n çhiass ceaghlagh,” dooyrt Hester. “Lhisagh shin jeeaghyn er.” Ren ad y soo y aarlaghey dy kiart, as va'n soo blasstal.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ren Hester y ynsaghey ec y colleish?
Ren ee jeshaghteyrys y ynsaghey.
Cre ta 'sy gass?
She meetane eh.
Vel xenon lostey myr meetane?
Cha nel. Cha nel xenon lostey.
Cre ta fo'n thalloo ec y fungys?
Ta snaueyn banglaneagh ec y fungys fo'n thalloo.
Cre'n fa ta laue fuygh er y saagh?
Er-y-fa nagh vel fuygh leeideilagh.

lessons.title: Shibbyr son y buinney
lessons.summary: Myfanwy Treharne, a trustee of a small parish church in the south, organises the harvest supper: the parish council has paid to widen the hall, the priest Augustine Pell leads a liturgical service with a hymn about heaven, and at long tables the people of the parish eat together, which she sees as the fulfilment of a year's work and of an old friendship.
lessons.text:
Ta Myfanwy Treharne cummal ayns skylley beg 'sy jiass jeh'n ellan. Ta keeil veg shenn 'sy skylley, as ta Myfanwy ny treishteilagh jeh'n cheeil. Ta kiare treishteilee ec y cheeil. Ta ny treishteilee jeeaghyn lurg y thie, yn argid as ny lioaryn.

Dagh fouyr, lurg y buinney, ta shibbyr mooar ayns y cheeil son sleih ny skylley. Ta Myfanwy reaghey y shibbyr dagh blein. Roish nish, va'n thie beg ry-lhiattee rish y cheeil ro veg son y shibbyr. Er-y-fa shen, hug y chionnal argid son y thie y lheanaghey. Ta'n chionnal ny possan dy leih ta reill y skylley. Ren troggeyderyn gobbraghey 'sy tourey, as nish ta'n thie lheanit. T'eh daa cheayrt cho mooar as v'eh.

Er yn oie jeh'n shibbyr, haink sleih veih dagh thie 'sy skylley. Hoshiaght, va shirveish 'sy cheeil. Ren y saggyrt, Augustine Pell, y shirveish y leeid. She shirveish liturgagh v'ayn, as va'n saggyrt jannoo ymmyd jeh shenn lioar liturgagh. “Ta mee er ve leeid shirveishyn rish feed blein,” dooyrt eh rish Myfanwy, “as she yn shirveish shoh yn shirveish share 'sy vlein.”

Ren ny sleih arrane y ghoaill mychione niau. Ayns yn arrane, ta niau ny ynnyd jeh soilshey as shee. Va Myfanwy goaill yn arrane dy ard. Er yn oie shen, va Myfanwy smooinaghtyn nagh row niau foddey veih'n cheeil.

Lurg y shirveish, hie dy chooilley pheiagh stiagh 'sy thie lheanit. Va boayrd liauyr ayn, as er y voayrd va feill, praaseyn, arran, caashey as peeshyn mooarey. Va sleih shenn as sleih aeg ny soie ry-cheilley. Va caarjys ayn: va caarjyn loayrt as gearey, as va paitçhyn roie mygeayrt.

Dooyrt Augustine rish Myfanwy: “She cooilleeiney eh y shibbyr shoh. Ta'n obbyr ec ny eirinee er jerrey, as ta'n buinney 'sy thie. She cooilleeiney blein slane v'ayn.”

“As she cooilleeiney jeh caarjys shenn,” dooyrt Myfanwy. “Va my voir as my ayr ec y shibbyr shoh roish daeed blein. Ta'n chaarjys eddyr sleih ny skylley foast lajer.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Myfanwy ec y cheeil?
T'ee ny treishteilagh jeh'n cheeil.
Quoi hug argid son y thie y lheanaghey?
Hug y chionnal argid son y thie y lheanaghey.
Quoi ren y shirveish y leeid?
Ren y saggyrt, Augustine Pell, y shirveish y leeid.
Cre va ayns yn arrane?
Va'n arrane mychione niau.
Cre dooyrt Augustine mychione y shibbyr?
Dooyrt eh dy row y shibbyr cooilleeiney blein slane.

lessons.title: Bee 'sy scoill
lessons.summary: Delphine Marchbank, a mother in Ramsey, sees a documentary broadcast on TV about poor school dinners and becomes a candidate in the election; her campaign calls for reforms, especially for the small provincial schools, and in a dispute with a minister on the radio she stays diplomatic, which people see as leadership.
lessons.text:
Ta Delphine Marchbank cummal ayns Rhumsaa, as ta daa phaitçhey eck 'sy vunscoill. Roish blein, va claare feanishagh mychione bee 'sy scoill goll er creeley er y çhellveeish. Ren y claare feanishagh soilshaghey dy row drogh vee ayns ram scoillyn: bee feayr, bee gyn blass, as monney shugyr ayn. Va'n claare goll er creeley ec shiaght er y chlag 'sy fastyr, as va ram sleih jeeaghyn er.

Va Delphine jeeaghyn er y chlaare feanishagh. Lurg shen, cha dod ee cadley. “Lhisagh red ennagh caghlaa,” dooyrt ee rish e sheshey. “As my nagh jean peiagh erbee eh, nee'm eh hene.”

'Sy tourey, va reihys ayn. Haink Delphine dy ve ny enmyssagh. Cha row ee rieau ayns politickaght roie. Va kiare persoonyn elley ayns y reihys, as va dagh enmyssagh elley er ve ayns politickaght rish blein as blein. Va Delphine yn enmyssagh s'aeg.

Ren Delphine goaill toshiaght er e troddan. She troddan beg v'ayn, agh va'n troddan feer lajer. Hie ee veih dorrys gys dorrys, as loayr ee rish sleih mychione bee ny paitçhyn. “Ta aalhiasseeyn feme orrin,” dooyrt ee. “Ta feme ain er bee çheh as bee mie dagh laa. Ta feme ain er aalhiasseeyn ayns y reiltys myrgeddin.”

Ren ee loayrt er lheh mychione ny scoillyn queiggagh. Ayns ny scoillyn queiggagh beggey ayns ny glionteeyn, cha nel thie-bee ayn ec y scoill hene, as ta'n bee çheet ayns gleashtan veih Doolish. Tra t'eh roshtyn y scoill queiggagh, t'eh feayr. “Ta ny aalhiasseeyn shoh scanshoil son ny scoillyn queiggagh, er lheh,” dooyrt ee.

Laa dy row, va Delphine er y radio marish oltey jeh'n reiltys. Va streean eddyr oc. Dooyrt yn oltey dy row y bee 'sy scoill mie dy liooar, as nagh row y claare feanishagh kiart. Va'n streean feer çheh. Agh cha dooyrt Delphine drogh fockle erbee. V'ee diploamagh. “Ta mee toiggal nagh vel monney argid ec y reiltys,” dooyrt ee. “Agh lhisagh shin jannoo yn obbyr shoh ry-cheilley.”

Va sleih clashtyn y streean er y radio. Va ram jeu booiagh dy row Delphine cho diploamagh. “Shen stiureydys,” dooyrt fer-pabyr-naight. “Cha nel stiureydys mychione ve ard. T'eh mychione ve kiart as diploamagh.”

Lurg mee, hooar Delphine ny smoo voteyn na dagh enmyssagh elley. Nish, t'ee gobbraghey er ny aalhiasseeyn ayns y reiltys.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va'n claare feanishagh soilshaghey?
Va'n claare soilshaghey dy row drogh vee ayns ram scoillyn.
Cre'n fa ta'n bee feayr ayns ny scoillyn queiggagh?
Er-y-fa dy vel y bee çheet ayns gleashtan veih Doolish.
Cre dooyrt oltey yn reiltys ayns y streean?
Dooyrt eh dy row y bee mie dy liooar, as nagh row y claare kiart.
Row Delphine diploamagh?
Va. Cha dooyrt ee drogh fockle erbee.
Cre dooyrt y fer-pabyr-naight mychione stiureydys?
Dooyrt eh dy vel stiureydys mychione ve kiart as diploamagh.

lessons.title: Fungyssyn 'sy ghlion
lessons.summary: Ezra Penrose and his wife Tabitha come from England for the motorsport week; in a glen he picks wild mushrooms while she warns that some are deadly and shows him a chrysalis on a leaf; that night he is sick with pain in his torso and is filled with horror, they wait in the hospital while he endures the pain, and the doctor finds it was not a deadly mushroom.
lessons.text:
Dagh blein, ta Ezra Penrose as e ven, Tabitha, çheet veih Sostyn gys Ellan Vannin son shiaghtin y spoyrt gleashtanagh. Ta Ezra feer laccal y spoyrt gleashtanagh. T'eh jeeaghyn er ny gleashtanyn tappee rish ooryn. Cha nel Tabitha cho laccal y spoyrt gleashtanagh. She bee as dooghys share lhee.

Er y laa jerrinagh, hie ad son shooyl ayns glion. Va'n glion fliugh as feayr, as va fungyssyn gaase fo ny biljyn. “Lhig dooin fungyssyn y hroggal son y shibbyr,” dooyrt Ezra.

“Kiarail,” dooyrt Tabitha. “Ta ram fungyssyn marrooagh ayns ny glionteeyn. Ta paart jeu jeeaghyn myr fungyssyn mie, agh t'ad marrooagh.”

“Ta fys aym er fungyssyn,” dooyrt Ezra. Va Tabitha jeeaghyn er duillag. “Jeeagh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta cryslid er y duillag shoh.” Va'n cryslid beg as glass. “Ayns y cryslid shoh, ta foillycan çheet dy ve,” dooyrt ee. “Lurg tammylt, hig y foillycan magh ass y chryslid.” Va Ezra jeeaghyn er y chryslid son minnid, as eisht v'eh troggal fungyssyn reesht.

'Sy fastyr, ren Ezra ny fungyssyn y choagyrey, as dooyrt eh dy row ad blasstal. Cha ren Tabitha ad y ee. Ec mean-oie, va Ezra çhing. Va'n colb echey feer çhing, as va'n colb çheh. “Ta mee feer çhing,” dooyrt eh. Haink scoagh er Tabitha. Va scoagh urree dy row ny fungyssyn marrooagh.

Hie ad gys y thie-lheihys ayns Doolish. Va ram sleih çhing ayns y thie-lheihys, as v'ad fuirree. “Lhisagh shiu fuirree,” dooyrt y ven ec y dorrys. Ren ad fuirree rish three ooryn. Va colb Ezra çhing rish y traa ooilley. Cha row eh aashagh dy surr y çhingys, agh ren eh surranse eh. Va Tabitha cummal e laue.

'Sy jerrey, haink y fer-lheihys. Ren eh shilley er colb Ezra, as ghow eh fuill. “Cha nel ny fungyssyn shoh marrooagh,” dooyrt eh. “Ta dty volg çhing, agh bee oo mie ayns laa ny ghaa. Va ny fungyssyn shenn, as va paart jeu gyn coagyrey dy liooar.” Va Tabitha booiagh, as va Ezra booiagh myrgeddin, ga dy row eh foast çhing.

Lurg shen, cha row Ezra troggal fungyssyn ny smoo. Nish, t'eh kionnaghey fungyssyn ayns y shapp.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta Ezra as Tabitha çheet gys Ellan Vannin?
T'ad çheet son shiaghtin y spoyrt gleashtanagh.
Cre honnick Tabitha er y duillag?
Honnick ee cryslid beg glass er y duillag.
Cre va çhing ec Ezra?
Va'n colb echey çhing.
Cre cho liauyr as ren ad fuirree ayns y thie-lheihys?
Ren ad fuirree rish three ooryn.
Row ny fungyssyn marrooagh?
Cha row. Cha row ny fungyssyn marrooagh.

lessons.title: Laa 'sy sniaghtey
lessons.summary: On a day of leisure in the snow, Clem Haverford takes his six-year-old daughter Juniper and her doll up the hill with a sledge and a picnic: he pushes the sledge, it breaks on a stone and her trousers get wet, and by a frozen pool they drink hot soup, eat bread and feed the crumbs to the pigeons.
lessons.text:
Va sniaghtey er ny sleityn ayns y gheurey. Va Clem Haverford gyn obbyr er y Jesarn shen, as va laa soccar echey. “Ta laa soccar aym jiu,” dooyrt eh rish e inneen, Juniper. “Lhig dooin goll seose er y slieau.” Ta Juniper shey bleeaney d'eash, as t'ee goaill e babban marish dy chooilley raad. Ghow ee y babban jiu myrgeddin.

Ren Clem soo çheh y aarlaghey, as hug eh soo, arran as caashey ayns kishtey. Eisht ghow eh yn shenn sleayd veih'n thie beg cooylloo y thie. She sleayd fuygh v'ayn. Va'n sleayd shoh ec Clem hene tra v'eh beg.

Er y slieau, va'n sniaghtey bane as bog. Hoie Juniper er y sleayd, as ghow ee y babban 'sy laue eck. “Saih mee, Ayr!” dooyrt ee. Ren Clem y sleayd y heiy, as hie'n sleayd sheese dy tappee. Va Juniper gearey dy ard. “Reesht! Saih mee reesht!” dooyrt ee. Ren Clem y sleayd y heiy keayrt as keayrt.

Agh 'sy jerrey, va clagh fo'n sniaghtey. Vrish y sleayd er y chlagh, as huitt Juniper ayns y sniaghtey. Vrish yn shenn sleayd ayns daa ayrn. Cha row lhott erbee er Juniper, agh va'n sniaghtey ayns e breeçhyn, as va ny breeçhyn eck fliugh as feayr. Va'n babban ayns y sniaghtey myrgeddin. “Vrish yn sleayd!” dooyrt ee, as ren ee keayney.

Ghow Clem y babban, as ren eh y sniaghtey y ghlenney jeh. “Ta'n babban mie,” dooyrt eh. “As ta mee goll dy chiartaghey y sleayd.”

V'ad goll sheese reesht, as haink ad gys lhingey beg. Va rio er y lhingey. “Ny brish y rio!” dooyrt Clem, tra hug Juniper e chass er. “Ta'n lhingey feayr fo'n rio.” Hoie ad ec oirr y lhingey, as d'ee ad y soo çheh as yn arran. Va'n soo çheh mie son breeçhyn fliugh!

Haink calmaneyn gys y lhingey. Va ny calmaneyn shirrey bee 'sy sniaghtey. Hug Juniper meeryn arran da ny calmaneyn. Haink calmane beg glass faggys dy liooar dy ghoaill yn arran ass e laue.

'Sy fastyr, ren Clem y sleayd y chiartaghey, as hug Juniper breeçhyn elley urree. “Va shoh yn laa soccar share,” dooyrt ee.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va laa soccar ec Clem?
Er-y-fa nagh row obbyr echey er y Jesarn shen.
Cre ghow Juniper marish?
Ghow ee e babban marish.
Cre haghyr da'n sleayd?
Vrish y sleayd er clagh fo'n sniaghtey.
Cre va er y lhingey?
Va rio er y lhingey.
Cre hug Juniper da ny calmaneyn?
Hug ee meeryn arran da ny calmaneyn.
